previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of sclerosing mesenteritis and 23 prior abdominal surgeries was admitted for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and high G-tube output, consistent with a chronic partial small bowel obstruction due to adhesions. She was managed conservatively with G-tube decompression, TPN, IV fluids, and rectal Dilaudid for pain control. An upper endoscopy confirmed a tight proximal obstruction that could not be traversed, and a small bowel follow-through showed stable findings without complete obstruction. Her tachycardia improved with hydration. Pain control was optimized with a compounded rectal Dilaudid formulation for outpatient use, and her IV fluid regimen was increased to 3 liters daily to prevent future admissions. She was discharged home with services in stable condition, with plans for ongoing TPN, fluid support, and close outpatient follow-up.
problems: Intestinal or peritoneal adhesions with obstruction (postoperative) (postinfection)

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Abdomen, supine and upright views.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ female with history of multiple past bowel
surgeries complaining of one day of abdominal pain, vomiting, concerned that
she has bowel obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors including ___. 

As also seen on prior study from ___, there are multiple air-dilated
loops of colon with air seen to the level of the rectum.  Multiple air-fluid
levels are seen in the upright view, difficult to discern whether colon or
small bowel.  Again seen is a right femoral line ending in the hepatic IVC. 
There is a pigtail catheter projecting over the left upper quadrant.  Multiple
surgical clips are seen in the right abdomen.  No definite evidence of free
air is seen although the left hemidiaphragm is not fully included.

IMPRESSION:  As seen previously, bowel dilatation with some air-fluid levels,
may relate to patient's chronic partial bowel obstruction.

On further examination the Tip of the catheter was assesed to be in the distal
cavo atrial Junction

INDICATION:  ___ woman with chronic right femoral ___ catheter. 
The catheter has a hole and that needs to be repaired/replaced.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ (fellow) performed the procedure.  Dr.
___ (attending physician) was present and supervised throughout
the procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
50 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of Versed throughout the total intraservice time
of 35 minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored.

PROCEDURE:  Written informed consent was obtained from the patient after
explaining the risks, benefits and alternatives of the procedure.  The right
thigh along with indwelling ___ catheter were prepped and draped in a
sterile fashion.  A preprocedural huddle and timeout were performed per ___
protocol.

The catheter was initially attempted to be repaired but even after placing a
new repaired line there was no flushing that could be achieved through one of
the ports and it was still leaking at the junction site.  It was assumed that
one of the lumens was clogged and the backpressure was causing the catheter to
leak.  A decision was made to exchange the indwelling catheter.

Initial scout fluoroscopic image demonstrated the indwelling catheter to be in
the right atrium.  Under aseptic conditions, a 0.018 SV8 wire was passed
through one of the ports into the right atrium.  The catheter was removed over
a wire to place a 4 ___ C2 glide catheter.  Appropriate measurements were
made.  The 0.018 was exchanged for a 0.035 Amplatz.  The glide catheter was
exchanged for a long 10 ___ peel-away sheath that was placed under
fluoroscopy.  The inner cannula and wire were removed to facilitate placement
of a new 10 ___ 46-cm central venous catheter.  Sheath was peeled away. 
The catheter tip was confirmed under fluoroscopy to be at the right atrium. 
Cuff was placed within the tunnel about 2-3 cm from the skin incision. 
Catheter was secured by 0 Prolene sutures.  0 Prolene pursestring suture was
placed within the incision.  Site was appropriately dressed.  The catheter was
flushed and withdrew well.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
post-procedural complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful uncomplicated fluoroscopic guidance exchange of an old
10 ___ 46-cm tunneled right femoral central venous catheter with a similar
46-cm 10 ___ tunneled Hickman.  The tip is in the right atrium.  The line
is ready to use.

INDICATION:  ___ female with recent replacement of right femoral
Hickman catheter, now with superficial right leg pain from thigh to the knee.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and duplex Doppler ultrasound examination of the right
lower extremity veins was performed.

FINDINGS:  The right common femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal veins
demonstrate normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation.  Flow is
demonstrated in the right posterior tibial and peroneal veins.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence for DVT in right lower extremity.

INDICATION:  ___ female with recent right femoral Hickman replacement
for chronic TPN, here to evaluate Hickman placement.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph, last performed on ___.

PORTABLE FRONTAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  There has been interval placement of a
Hickman catheter coursing above the diaphragm.  The tip of the line is not
well visualized due to technique, but appears to project over the atrium.  A
repeat radiograph with abdominal technique could be considered to confirm this
finding.  

A gastrostomy catheter is again seen below the diaphragm terminating in the
left upper quadrant.  A spinal stimulator device is unchanged in appearance. 
The right hemidiaphragm is slightly elevated, which may be related to poor
inspiratory effort.  The lungs are clear without focal consolidation, pleural
effusion, or pneumothorax.  The pulmonary vasculature is not engorged.  The
cardiac silhouette is normal in size.  The mediastinal and hilar contours are
within normal limits.
